data.name: Darwesh
data.gender_notes: Darwesh is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A person who is deeply knowledgeable and wise, a scholar or a teacher. The name Darwesh carries the meaning “Wise, Knowledgeable” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Darwesh usually hope their child will grow to embody wise, knowledgeable and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A seeker of knowledge on the spiritual path, a spiritual guide
data.etymology: Darwesh belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wise, Knowledgeable.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Darwesh total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_arabic.name: درويش
in_arabic.meaning: درويش تعني الفقير أو المتعفف عن الدنيا
in_arabic.long_meaning: درويش هو الشخص الذي يتقنع بالفقر و يترك الدنيا و ملذاتها، و هو من الأسماء التي تعبر عن التواضع و الزهد في الحياة الدنيا، و يرتبط هذا الاسم بالعديد من الشخصيات التاريخية في الإسلام، مثل درويش الرومي الذي كان شاعرا و مفكرا إسلاميا مشهورا.

in_urdu.name: درویش
in_urdu.meaning: درویش کا مطلب ہے فقیر یا دنیا سے توکل کرنے والا
in_urdu.long_meaning: درویش وہ شخص ہوتا ہے جو فقیر ہونے کا انتخاب کرتا ہے اور دنیا کی لذتیں ترک کر دیتا ہے، یہ نام تواضع اور دنیا سے منسلک ہونے سے دور رہنے کی علامت ہے، یہ نام جنوبی ایشیا میں خاص طور پر مشہور ہے جہاں صوفیاء اور فقیر حضرات اس نام کو اپناتے ہیں.

in_hindi.name: दरवीश
in_hindi.meaning: दरवीश का अर्थ है فقیر या दुनिया से विमुख होने वाला
in_hindi.long_meaning: दरवीश वह व्यक्ति होता है जो فقیر बनने का चुनाव करता है और दुनिया की لذتیں त्याग देता है, यह नाम विनम्रता और दुनिया से अलग रहने का प्रतीक है, यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में विशेष रूप से प्रसिद्ध है जहां सूफी संत और فقیر इस नाम को अपनाते हैं.

in_pashto.name: درويش
in_pashto.meaning: درويش يعني فقير يا دنياديدہ شخص
in_pashto.long_meaning: درويش هغه کسان دي چې په خپل اختيار سره فقير يي او د دنياد لذتونو څخه يي انصراف کوي، دا نوم د تواضع او د دنياوي چارو څخه د ليري والي نښه ده، دا نوم په افغانستان او پاکستان کې د پښتنو په منځ کې مشهور دی چيرته چې صوفيان او فقيران دا نوم اختياروي.

in_english.name: Darwesh
in_english.meaning: Sufi ascetic, one who renounces worldly pleasures
in_english.long_meaning: The name Darwesh originates from the Arabic root 'D-R-W-SH' which means 'to visit' or 'to frequent'. In the context of Sufism, a Darwesh refers to a Sufi ascetic who frequently visits spiritual gatherings and has renounced worldly pleasures. Historically, Darweshes were known for their piety, spiritual practices, and their role in spreading Islamic teachings through poetry and music.

pronunciation.pashto: په پښتو کې د تلفظ تفصیل: درويش

data.cultural_impact: The term "Darwesh" is rooted in Islamic culture and society as it reflects the deeply thoughtful and educated individuals who have devoted their lives to learning and teaching. These individuals were often seen as spiritual leaders and guides, contributing to the continuous preservation and transmission of Islamic knowledge, values, and traditions. Darweshes played crucial roles in various aspect of Islamic civilization, such as medicine, mathematics, astronomy, poetry, and philosophy. Their influence extended beyond the boundaries of the Islamic world, inspiring and shaping other civilizations and religions.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the term "Darwesh" can be seen in the profound and transformational role these individuals played in the lives of their students and communities. They were not just bearers of knowledge, but embodiments of wisdom and compassion. Their teachings, rooted in the Islamic tradition, offered guidance and solace for the spiritual journey of self-discovery and growth. The term "Darwesh" thus carries the essence of the unending quest for knowledge and truth, reminding us of the importance of seeking wisdom and wisdom in our own lives.
